methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Bubble Robotics is a robotics and manufacturing company at an undisclosed stage, founded by Jean Crosetti and Patricia Apostol. The valuation universe consists of 10 same-sector peers: one public company (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

Peer-median methodology was not applicable to this analysis. Despite identifying 10 competitors within Robotics & Manufacturing, none met the minimum threshold of three datapoints when filtered by stage proximity or valuation tier. The absence of same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables—critical for reducing noise in early-stage valuations—rendered a narrow peer-median approach unreliable. An all-sector median would have introduced substantial error given the heterogeneity typical in robotics subsectors.

The analysis therefore cannot support a specific valuation range through triangulation. The primary constraint is insufficient depth within narrow peer cohorts rather than absence of sector peers. To enable defensible valuation, additional stage-aligned comparables or direct financial metrics from the target (revenue, ARR, burn rate, or capital efficiency) would be required. The public comp and eight private peers remain available for monitoring as the company's profile becomes more defined or comparable datapoints emerge.
